finding.claim: Unauthenticated GET /rss passes the full attacker-supplied URL from params[:u] to open-uri's URI.open, which fetches it server-side with no scheme, host, IP, port, or redirect validation, and returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the caller. This allows full-read SSRF to internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.source: app.rb:7-8, params[:u] from the query string of GET /rss (no auth guard; the app has no before-filter or middleware)
finding.sink: app.rb:8 URI.open(params[:u]).read (open-uri performs the HTTP request and follows redirects)

trace.note: Unauthenticated route get "/rss" accepts any caller.
params[:u] is passed unmodified to URI.open, which, for a string matching scheme://, calls URI.parse(name).open and performs the HTTP(S) request from the server.
The response body is truncated to 400 bytes and returned to the attacker, so the SSRF is readable, not blind.

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, no parsed-host check, no private/loopback/link-local/metadata IP block, no port restriction, no scheme restriction, no redirect re-validation (open-uri follows http/https redirects to any host), no DNS pinning, no auth guard on the route. The only check in the file is the TRUSTED allowlist at app.rb:14, which exists only on /trusted and is not applied to /rss.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the TRUSTED host allowlist at app.rb:14, which is inside the /trusted route (app.rb:12-16) and is not applied to /rss (app.rb:7-10). No scheme, host, IP, port, or redirect validation exists anywhere in app.rb.
verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes the unvalidated query parameter params[:u] to URI.open(...).read, and app.rb:9 returns data[0, 400] to the caller, on a route (app.rb:7) with no auth or guard, so the SSRF is unauthenticated and readable.
